match.reason: The closest bank point is a Year 12 NSW card about mammal extinction that also covers land clearing, which is broader and at a different depth than this Year 9-10 point on introduced species spreading, outcompeting natives and damaging environments.

draft.title: Introduced species
card: An introduced species is a plant or animal brought by people from another place, on purpose or by accident. Rabbits, foxes, cats and cane toads are introduced to Australia.
Some introduced species spread fast. They can find plenty of food and have few predators or diseases to keep their numbers down.
They can damage environments in two main ways. They may outcompete native species for food, water and shelter, or they may eat native species.

Foxes and cats prey on small native animals. Rabbits eat plants that native animals need, and their grazing can leave soil bare. Cane toads are poisonous to many native predators that try to eat them.
draft.remember: Introduced species can spread fast and harm natives by competing with them or eating them.

a.q: What makes a plant or animal an introduced species in Australia?
opts: People brought it from another place
It is found in only one part of Australia
It moved into a new area after a bushfire
It eats other animals to survive
a.why: An introduced species is one that people have brought from elsewhere, on purpose or by accident. Moving within Australia after a fire is natural movement, not introduction, which is the most tempting wrong option.
a.clue: Think about where it came from and who moved it.

b.q: Rabbits were released on a farm near Hamilton and their numbers grew quickly. They now eat the grasses that native wallabies feed on. Why are the rabbits harming the wallabies?
opts: They outcompete the wallabies for food
They hunt and kill the wallabies
They bring in plants from other places
They are poisonous to the wallabies
b.why: The rabbits eat the same grasses, so there is less food for the wallabies. That is competition. The rabbits do not hunt wallabies, so the option about killing them is wrong, even though introduced predators such as foxes do harm natives that way.
b.clue: What do the rabbits and wallabies both need?

a.best: People brought it from another place

b.best: They outcompete the wallabies for food

problems.detail: The card says introduced species damage environments in 'two main ways' (outcompeting or eating natives), then gives cane toads, which harm natives by poisoning predators that eat them, and rabbits leaving soil bare. Neither fits those two ways, which could confuse students. The remember line repeats the two-way split.
